pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 7.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can we pick ideas from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify main ideas in a reading text based on the theme for comprehension
2. use vocabulary based on the theme to construct sentences for communication
3. recognise the value of reading texts for information in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information

Teach
• Focus skill: identify main ideas in a reading text based on the theme for comprehension.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we pick ideas from a text?
2. How can we identify talents and gifts among people?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
